Project: Django. Upgrade being assessed: 3.2 -> 4.2.
This change was introduced in release 4.2. Source: Django 4.2 release notes (official_release_notes). Section: Django 4.2 release notes / Features deprecated in 4.2 / Passing encoded JSON string literals to JSONField is deprecated.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): [
 {
  "release": "4.2",
  "field": "python",
  "value": ">=3.8",
  "source_id": "dj_pypi@4.2",
  "json_path": "info.requires_python"
 }
]

ITEM:
<<<
JSONField and its associated lookups and aggregates used to allow passing JSON encoded string literals which caused ambiguity on whether string literals were already encoded from database backend's perspective. During the deprecation period string literals will be attempted to be JSON decoded and a warning will be emitted on success that points at passing non-encoded forms instead. Code that used to pass JSON encoded string literals: Document.objects.bulk_create( Document(data=Value("null")), Document(data=Value("[]")), Document(data=Value('"foo-bar"')), ) Document.objects.annotate( JSONBAgg("field", default=Value("[]")), )
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Django 4.2 release notes / Features deprecated in 4.2 / Passing encoded JSON string literals to JSONField is deprecated: JSONField and its associated lookups and aggregates used to allow passing JSON encoded string literals which caused ambiguity on whether string literals were already encoded from database backend's perspective. During the deprecation period string literals will be attempted to be JSON decoded and a warning will be emitted on success that points at passing non-encoded forms instead. Code that used to pass JSON encoded string literals: Document.objects.bulk_create( Document(data=Value("null")), Document(data=Value("[]")), Document(data=Value('"foo-bar"')), ) Document.objects.annotate( JSONBAgg("field", default=Value("[]")), ) Should become: Document.objects.bulk_create( Document(data=Value(None, JSONField())), Document(data=[]), Document(data="foo-bar"), ) Document.objects.annotate( JSONBAgg("field", default=[]), ) From Django 5.1+ string literals will be implicitly interpreted as JSON string literals.
>>>

paths.path_name: JSON-encoded string literals passed via Value() to JSONField
paths.description: JSONField and its lookups used to accept JSON-encoded string literals such as Value("null"), Value("[]") or Value('"foo-bar"'). During the 4.2 deprecation period Django tries to JSON-decode such string literals and emits a warning if decoding succeeds. From Django 5.1 string literals will be implicitly interpreted as JSON string literals, which changes their meaning.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 4.2, where passing encoded JSON string literals is deprecated (current version below 4.2).
quotes: During the deprecation period string literals will be attempted to be JSON decoded
conditions.relevance: Ties the deprecation and warning behavior to the 4.2 release.

conditions.statement: The application passes JSON-encoded string literals wrapped in Value() to a JSONField, for example in bulk_create, create or update.
conditions.expected_value: Value("<JSON-encoded string>") assigned to a JSONField
quotes: JSONField and its associated lookups and aggregates used to allow passing JSON encoded string literals
conditions.relevance: Only code that passes encoded string literals triggers the warning and the later change in meaning.
ambiguities: The text shows bulk_create examples but does not say which other operations are affected beyond 'lookups and aggregates'.

suggested_actions: Replace Value("[]") with the plain Python value [].
Replace Value('"foo-bar"') with the plain Python string "foo-bar".
Run tests with deprecation warnings enabled to find remaining encoded string literals.

paths.path_name: JSON-encoded string default passed to JSONBAgg
paths.description: Aggregates such as JSONBAgg used to accept JSON-encoded string literals as defaults, for example default=Value("[]"). During the 4.2 deprecation period these are JSON-decoded with a warning. From Django 5.1 string literals will be implicitly interpreted as JSON string literals.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 4.2, where passing encoded JSON string literals is deprecated (current version below 4.2).
quotes: During the deprecation period string literals will be attempted to be JSON decoded
conditions.relevance: Ties the deprecation and warning behavior to the 4.2 release.

conditions.statement: The application passes a JSON-encoded string literal in Value() as the default of JSONBAgg or another JSON aggregate.
conditions.relevance: This is the aggregate form named as affected by the deprecation.

suggested_actions: Replace default=Value("[]") with default=[] in JSONBAgg calls.
Run tests with deprecation warnings enabled to find remaining encoded string defaults.
